rejection.pageSubtitle: Choose the message closest to what you received.

vehicleNotFound.title: Vehicle Not Found
vehicleNotFound.cause: The registration number entered doesn't match any record the system recognises.
vehicleNotFound.explanation: This usually happens when a letter, number or dash is slightly off, or the vehicle was registered very recently.
vehicleNotFound.resolution: Use the Validator tool to check your format, compare it carefully with your registration book, and try again.

simCnicMismatch.title: SIM CNIC Mismatch
simCnicMismatch.cause: The CNIC linked to the SIM you used doesn't match the CNIC on file for the application.
simCnicMismatch.explanation: Mobile networks register each SIM to one CNIC. If you're using someone else's SIM, the names won't line up.
simCnicMismatch.resolution: Send the SMS from a SIM registered in your own name, or ask the SIM owner to apply using their own details.

alreadyRegistered.title: Already Registered
alreadyRegistered.cause: This vehicle has already been registered for this relief cycle.
alreadyRegistered.explanation: Sending the SMS more than once does not create duplicate registrations — the system keeps only the first one.
alreadyRegistered.resolution: No action needed. If you believe this is wrong, contact the official helpline from the Contact page.

invalidRegNumber.title: Invalid Registration Number
invalidRegNumber.cause: The format of the registration number doesn't match what the system expects for your province.
invalidRegNumber.explanation: Each province has its own plate pattern. A missing dash or extra space is a common cause.
invalidRegNumber.resolution: Check the Province Guide for an example from your province, then try again with the corrected format.

rejection.recentNote: Still stuck? Open the AI Assistant and describe exactly what the SMS reply said.

punjab.name: Punjab
punjab.dateLocation: Printed on the first inside page, next to "Date of Registration".
steps: Open your vehicle registration book to the first page.
Look for the field labelled "Date of Registration" near the top.
The date is written as DD-MM-YYYY.
If the page is faded, check the excise office stamp — the date is usually repeated there.

sindh.name: Sindh
sindh.dateLocation: Found on the particulars page, under "Registration Date".
steps: Open the book to the particulars page (usually page 2).
Find "Registration Date" in the left-hand column.
Note the date exactly as printed, including the year.
Older books may show the date in the top-right stamp instead.

kpk.name: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
kpk.dateLocation: Listed under "Tareekh-e-Register" near the vehicle details box.
steps: Open to the vehicle details box on the first page.
Find the Urdu/English bilingual line for registration date.
Convert the date to DD-MM-YYYY format if needed.
Keep the book handy — some offices ask for a photo of this page.

balochistan.name: Balochistan
balochistan.dateLocation: Printed beside the owner's details on the inside cover.
steps: Open the inside front cover.
The registration date sits beside the owner's name and CNIC.
Double-check the year — books printed near a year-end are easy to misread.
If unclear, the excise receipt kept with the book usually has the same date.

islamabad.name: Islamabad
islamabad.dateLocation: Shown on the smart card, or the booklet for older registrations.
steps: If you have a smart card, the date is on the back, bottom row.
If you have the older booklet, check the first printed page.
The format is DD-MM-YYYY.
Keep a copy of this number handy before using the Validator tool.

help.q: What can Fuel Relief Assistant help me with?
help.a: Checking your registration details, understanding rejection messages, estimating eligibility, and finding your registration date — explained in plain language.

ready.q: What information should I keep ready?
ready.a: Your vehicle registration book and the province it was issued in. You do not need to share your CNIC with this platform.

phone.q: Can I use this service on my phone?
phone.a: Yes. This help desk is designed for phones, slow connections, and people using the internet for the first time.

official.q: Is this an official government website?
official.a: No. This platform provides guidance only. It is not connected to official government databases and cannot register you.

data.q: Does this platform store my personal information?
data.a: Your checks and chats are saved only on your own device, in your browser. Nothing is uploaded to a server.

wrong.q: What if my registration is rejected after I use this tool?
wrong.a: Open the Rejection Help page and select the message you received, or contact the official helpline on the Contact page.

contact.pageSubtitle: If this platform's tools can't resolve your issue, here is how to reach official channels.
processSteps: Re-check your format using the Validator tool.
Read the explanation on the Rejection Help page.
Wait a few minutes and try sending the SMS again.
If it still fails, contact the official helpline with your registration book ready.
contact.escalationTitle: If the helpline can't resolve it
contact.escalationBody: Ask for a complaint reference number, and note the date and time of your call. Provincial citizen portals can also log complaints formally.
contact.feedbackBody: This form is for feedback on this guidance tool — not for official registration complaints.
contact.feedbackThanks: Thank you — your feedback is saved on this device.
